Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:10:1.hebrew: המקדיש שדהו - פי' בקונט' דלא גרסינן "בשנת היובל", דבשנת היובל עצמה פליגי רב ושמואל בפרק אין מקדישין (ערכין דף כד. ושם). ומיהו ברוב ספרים גרסינן התם בסדר המשנה "בשנת היובל". וי"ל דבשנת היובל משמע שפיר שנה שאחר היובל, ולא שנת חמשים ממש, מדלא קתני "בשנת היובל עצמה" כדקאמר בפלוגתא דרב ושמואל. ואע"ג דכתיב "בשנת היובל ישוב השדה" וגו', והתם ע"כ בשנת היובל עצמה — יש לחלק: דלשון תורה לחוד, דקרא לאו אורחיה לכתוב "עצמה". והתם נמי יליף רב מדכתיב "ואם משנת היובל", ושנת היובל בכלל, ופריך ליה שמואל: מי כתיב "משנת היובל"?:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:10:1.english: One who consecrates his field - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that we do not read "in the year of the Jubilee," because Rav and Shmuel disagree about [a field consecrated in] the Jubilee year itself, in the chapter "Ein Makdishin" (Arakhin 24a and there). However, in most books we do read there, in the order of the Mishnah, "in the year of the Jubilee." And one can say that "in the year of the Jubilee" quite plausibly means the year after the Jubilee, and not the fiftieth year itself, since it does not teach "in the Jubilee year itself," as [the wording] is stated in the dispute of Rav and Shmuel. And although it is written, "In the year of the Jubilee the field shall return," etc., and there it must mean the Jubilee year itself — one can distinguish: the language of the Torah is a separate matter, as it is not the way of a verse to write "itself." And there too, Rav derives [his view] from the fact that it is written, "And if from the year of the Jubilee," and the Jubilee year is included; and Shmuel challenges him: Is it written "*from* the year of the Jubilee"?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:1:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן בניפלי - אין לפרש דלא חששו לבדוק במערה שניה אלא עד כ', דלא החמירו כולי האי לבדוק רק למערת הנפלים. מדפריך בתר הכי: "מדהך בניפלי, הנך נמי בניפלי", משמע דאותו שמצא מוקמי בניפלי. וקשה, דהא קתני "מארבע אמות ועד ח'", ומערת נפלים אינה אלא ו'. וצ"ל, דאף על גב דרישא איירי בגדולים, מכל מקום הא דקתני "ובודק ממנו ולהלן כ'" איירי בניפלי, ולא קאי ארישא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:1:1.english: "Here, with what are we dealing? With [a cave of] nefalim" - One cannot explain that they were not concerned to check in the second cave except up to twenty [cubits], because they were not so stringent as to check [at such a distance] except for a cave of nefalim (stillborn infants). [This is] since [the Gemara] asks afterward: "Since this one is [speaking] of nefalim, these also are [speaking] of nefalim," which implies that the one who found [the bones] is established as [dealing with] nefalim. And this is difficult, for [the Mishnah] teaches "from four cubits up to eight," yet a cave of nefalim is only six [cubits]. And one must say that even though the first clause deals with adults, nevertheless, that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "and he checks from there onward twenty [cubits]," deals with nefalim, and does not refer back to the first clause:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:9:1.hebrew: בית כור עפר - נראה דנקט עפר לרבותא, דאפי' הכי פחות מי' טפחים נמדדין עמה; ולא כמו שפירש הקונטרס, דאי לא אמר ליה עפר אלא בית כור סתם — אפי' כולן סלעים הגיעו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 102b:9:1.english: A beit kor of earth - It appears that [the Mishnah] specified "earth" to teach a novel point: that even so, [pits] of less than ten handbreadths are measured together with it; and not as the Kuntres (Rashi) explained. For if he had not said "earth" to him, but only a beit kor without specification, then even if all of it were rocky ground, it would count as having reached him [i.e., the buyer would have received his due].
